recommendation: Keep the empty external-repo audit commit as-is for FHIR-14090. No FHIR-core source follow-up is needed unless the cardinality prose becomes inaccurate; if a concrete validator or IG Publisher behavior problem remains, follow Grahame Grieve's Jira comment and raise it against HL7/fhir-ig-publisher or the validator implementation repository.
issue_request: FHIR-14090 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core STU3 change request about inconsistent IG Publisher and Forge handling of extension cardinality. The final resolution said validators should enforce both the cardinalities declared in an extension definition StructureDefinition and the cardinalities declared by a StructureDefinition that references the extension, and should report an error when referencing cardinalities fall outside the allowed bounds.
initial_application: No current git commit directly tagged FHIR-14090 was found in the FHIR-core source history. The relevant specification rule was already present in core source before this Jira was created: defining-extensions.html says extension-definition cardinality constraints apply wherever the extension is used, and explains that profiles may tighten but not exceed the extension's minimum and maximum cardinality bounds. The closest explicit source history is earlier cardinality-documentation work, including #10157 and FHIR-12413, not a source change for this tooling issue.
additional_context: Current profiling guidance also says profiles can restrict cardinality only within the limits of the constrained base structure, and the extension-use section says an extension's minimum cardinality in a profile must be a valid restriction on the extension definition. The current FHIR-core checkout has no Java validator or IG Publisher source; it depends on the external org.hl7.fhir.validation artifact, and the Jira's later comment says this is an old tooling issue that should be raised in the HL7/fhir-ig-publisher issue tracker if still reproducible. Related extension-cardinality issues FHIR-12413 and FHIR-14378 are already represented on the combined branch and support the same interpretation of extension-definition cardinality.
reconciliation: This reconciliation intentionally made no FHIR-core source change. The current core specification already states the cardinality rule needed for implementer understanding, and the requested enforcement behavior belongs to validator/IG Publisher tooling outside this repository rather than to a current build-scope core source file.
